summary.intent: Implement steps 11-13 of a Windows session-restore tool's core library: filter cloaked/own-process/Program Manager windows, read process exe path, and read command line plus parent PID via WMI. The user then asked that windows on other virtual desktops not be hidden.
summary.outcome: All three steps were implemented in Sessions.Core and verified against real windows; the cloak filter was then changed to keep windows on other virtual desktops (DWM_CLOAKED_SHELL) and drop only app-cloaked ones. Core builds clean (0 warnings/0 errors).

repo: Sessions.Core uses CsWin32, with APIs listed in src/Sessions.Core/NativeMethods.txt; generated bindings differ from raw Win32 names, e.g. OpenProcess_SafeHandle instead of OpenProcess, and GetWindowLong because the metadata has no GetWindowLongPtr.
Process lookups (exe path, WMI command line/parent PID) live in ProcessDetails.cs, separate from WindowEnumerator.cs.

WindowInfo carries ExePath, CommandLine, ParentProcessId and UnsupportedReason; on failure ExePath stays null and UnsupportedReason is set rather than guessing. Empty or missing command line becomes null.
System.Management 9.0.0 is used for WMI Win32_Process queries; WMI failures are caught and non-fatal, leaving CommandLine and ParentProcessId null.
Using the SafeHandle variant makes an explicit CloseHandle unnecessary, though CloseHandle remains in NativeMethods.txt per the spec.

code.finding: IsCloaked was renamed to IsAppCloaked. It reads DWMWA_CLOAKED but treats DWM_CLOAKED_SHELL (2, window on another virtual desktop) as not hidden; only app or inherited cloaking excludes a window. Exact line numbers were not given in the transcript.

ReadExePath uses OpenProcess_SafeHandle(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION) with QueryFullProcessImageName and a Span<char> overload; ReadWmi queries CommandLine and ParentProcessId from Win32_Process.

workflow: Verified behaviour with temporary scratchpad console projects against live windows and deleted them afterwards.

When the window count dropped unexpectedly from 7 to 2, the cause was found by confirming the processes were still running and then dumping raw DwmGetWindowAttribute values with a P/Invoke diagnostic, rather than assuming over-exclusion.
The assistant flagged the design consequence (cloaked filter hides other virtual desktops) up front, which led to the user's follow-up correction.

friction: The cloak filter as specified initially hid windows on other virtual desktops, which is wrong for a session-restore tool, and it took a diagnostic to find this.
CsWin32 API naming deviations (SafeHandle variants, GetWindowLong vs GetWindowLongPtr) forced departures from the spec's literal API names.
First build after the initial write needed a rewrite of ProcessDetails.cs to use the SafeHandle and Span overloads.
open_items: Decide whether 'Windows Input Experience', an always-present system window, should be filtered by name like Program Manager.
Decide whether to drop CloseHandle from NativeMethods.txt since the SafeHandle makes it unnecessary.

Commits are not yet made; suggested messages: feat(core): exclude cloaked and own-process windows; feat(core): read process executable path; feat(core): read command line and parent PID via WMI; fix(core): keep windows on other virtual desktops.
